about.title: Big Bear Lake Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Big Bear Lake sits in a mountain community where residents and the many seasonal visitors who come for the lake and slopes often rely on a smaller network of local urgent care clinics and the regional hospital, sometimes traveling down the mountain for specialized treatment. When a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mishandles medication, the effects can be serious — and confusing to sort through, especially with San Bernardino County's mix of local and out-of-area facilities involved. California law sets specific, tight deadlines and procedural steps for these claims, and a bad medical outcome by itself doesn't automatically mean malpractice occurred. If you believe a healthcare provider's negligence caused you harm, our team reviews the facts, consults with qualified medical experts as required, and explains whether you may have a case — at no cost to start.

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines
items.desc: California's MICRA rules generally require malpractice claims within one year of discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so timing matters.

items.title: Required Pre-Suit Notice
items.desc: Before filing, California law requires a 90-day notice to the healthcare provider. Our team is familiar with this process and can help make sure it's handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Standards
items.desc: Because a poor medical result alone isn't proof of malpractice, California cases almost always require review by a qualified medical expert. We can help arrange that evaluation and assess whether negligence played a role.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a malpractice claim after treatment in Big Bear Lake?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it happened. There's also a required 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider before a lawsuit can be filed. Because these deadlines are strict, it's worth having a case reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: I was treated at a small clinic here before being transferred down the mountain — does that complicate things?
items.answer: It can add extra steps, since more than one provider or facility may have been involved in your care. Our team can help sort out which providers' records and actions are relevant, whether the issue happened locally or after transfer for specialized treatment. This is a common situation in mountain communities like Big Bear Lake.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes, California law sets a cap on non-economic damages (like pain and suffering) in medical malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to this same cap. We can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation.
